A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HGT and gene losses are equally likely in the evolution of the prokaryotes and that the reconstructed gene content of LUCA might be sufficient for sustaining a functioning organism.
, in the evolution of the prokaryotes (and possibly also in eukaryotes), gene loss is a dominant force, which is approximately balanced by horizontal gene transfer.
the evolutionary history of prokaryote genomes is a history of gene loss and horizontal transfer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the notion of a tree of life should be re-interpretted as a trend in evolution rather than a full representation of it.
the reconstruction of evolutionary history is a complex task and that it should be approached with caution.
the species tree, which has been used to reconstruct the evolution of life forms, is a very crude approximation of the true evolutionary process.
